Thermal Barrier Coatings (TBCs) have been used in high thrust aircraft engines for many years.
TBCs have proved to be very effective in allowing higher turbine inlet temperatures in aircraft engines.
The life requirements for TBCs in aircraft engines are typically less than those required in industrial gas turbines.
The use of TBCs for industrial gas turbines can increase durability and longer service life if it can be successfully demonstrated.
This paper describes current and future applications of TBCs in industrial gas turbine engines.
The paper reviews the early testing and applications of TBCs.
The paper identifies and evaluates the areas of concern from the engine designer's and materials engineer's perspective when it comes to using TBCs in industrial gas turbines.
The key factors that are expected to influence the utilization of TBCs in advanced industrial gas turbine engines are the focus of the paper.
The paper anticipates the development of reliable, durable, and highly effective TBC systems.
The ultimate goal is to improve engine efficiency and performance through the use of TBCs in industrial gas turbine applications.
